sentences.text: The case of the plaintiffs, as per plaint, is that the plaintiffs are the legal heirs of Smt. Shakuntala Sethi, who was an NRI and having NRI Account bearing no.13521010000074 with the defendant/HDFC Bank.

It is averred that in the month of January, 2015, the deceased Smt.
Shakuntala Sethi requested the bank through email to provide her bank statement in respect of the aforesaid account for income tax purposes.
However, upon obtaining the bank statement, the deceased Smt. Shakuntala Sethi was shocked and surprised to note that a huge amount of Rs.12,49,000/- had been embezzled from her account.

As per the said statement, it was revealed that the following amounts were withdrawn from the account of the deceased Smt. Shakuntala Sethi during the period from 21.12.2012 to 26.12.2012:
 Rs.49,000/- on 21.12.2012 vide transaction no. 000000140008.
 Rs.2,00,000/- on 21.12.2012 vide transaction no. 000000140007.
 Rs.4,00,000/- on 21.12.2012 vide transaction no. 000000140006.
 Rs.6,00,000/- on 26.12.2012 vide transaction no. 000000140010.
2.
That the aforesaid withdrawals/embezzlement were carried out by way of cheques which were never issued or signed by the deceased Smt. Shakuntala Sethi in favour of any person.
The deceased Smt. Shakuntala Sethi made a complaint to the defendant bank and sought details of the said transactions, CSDJ No. 275/2020 Ms. Poonam Verma & Ors.
Vs. HDFC Bank Page no 2/ 17 stating that she had never issued any such cheques, vide letter dated 10.03.2015.
Thereafter, the said facts were brought to the notice of the Branch Manager of the defendant bank, who assured that the matter would be investigated.
He further assured the deceased Smt. Shakuntala Sethi and her son that the matter would be looked into and that the embezzled amount would be reverted shortly.
Owing to such assurances, the deceased Smt. Shakuntala Sethi did not report the matter to the police earlier, as she was under the impression that necessary action would be taken.

However,
when the deceased Smt. Shakuntala Sethi and her sons, namely Sh. Bhushan Kumar Sethi and Sh.
Gulshan Kumar Sethi, made enquiries from the concerned bank officials, including the head office of HDFC Bank, through emails and other communications, the matter was repeatedly delayed on one pretext or another.

It is further stated that the deceased Smt. Shakuntala Sethi never received any cheque book pertaining to the said series, and thus, the manipulation clearly appears to be on the part of the bank officials with a view to commit fraud and embezzle money from her account.
Left with no other option, the deceased Smt. Shakuntala Sethi lodged a complaint with the Commissioner of Police, PHQ, New Delhi on 02.07.2016, and also filed a complaint with the SHO,
P.S. Roop Nagar, New Delhi, which was duly received vide DD No. 32B dated 02.07.2016.

Smt.
Shakuntala Sethi, through her authorized representative (A.R.), had lodged an FIR against the defendants for the offences committed by them, but no action was taken on the complaint till date,
for reasons best known to the police authorities.
Aggrieved by the inaction of the police, the CSDJ No. 275/2020 Ms. Poonam Verma & Ors.

Vs. HDFC Bank Page no 3/ 17 deceased Smt. Shakuntala Sethi, through her A.R., filed a complaint under Section 200 read with Section 156(3) Cr.P.C.

sentences.text: Ld. Metropolitan Magistrate took cognizance of the complaint filed by the mother of the plaintiffs and directed the SHO, P.S. Roop Nagar, Delhi to file a status report in the matter.

That pursuant to the enquiry conducted in the matter regarding embezzlement from the account of the mother of the plaintiffs,
the IO filed a status report before the Court of Ms. Chetna Singh, Ld. ACMM, Tis Hazari Courts,
Delhi, vide report dated 05.07.2018, confirming the factum of four illegal/unauthorized transactions from the bank account of the deceased.
The said fact was accordingly confirmed to the deceased mother of the plaintiffs and the plaintiffs.
Consequently, the police of P.S. Roop Nagar, Delhi registered FIR No. 202/2018 dated 18.08.2018 under Section 420 IPC against the defendants and their officials, and investigation started.
Unfortunately, in the meantime, Smt. Shakuntala Sethi expired on 07.01.2020 at Brampton Civic Hospital, Brampton, Ontario, leaving behind the plaintiffs as her only legal heirs.
The plaintiffs inherited all the assets and liabilities of the deceased and have thus stepped into her shoes in respect of the aforesaid embezzled amount.
The plaintiffs, being the legal representatives of the deceased, are fully entitled to initiate proceedings against the defendants for the civil and criminal wrongs committed.
Despite the lapse of considerable time, the defendant bank has failed to refund the aforesaid amount of Rs. 12,49,000/- either during CSDJ No. 275/2020 Ms. Poonam Verma & Ors.
Vs. HDFC Bank Page no 4/ 17 the lifetime of the deceased or thereafter to the plaintiffs, who are the legal heirs of the deceased.
Hence, this suit.
3. Thereafter, summons of the present suit were issued upon the defendant.
Defendant was served and filed their WS.
The defendant has denied all the averments made in the plaint and submitted that the present suit is hopelessly barred by limitation.

It is further submitted that the Limitation Act, 1963 clearly provides that every suit instituted, appeal preferred, or application made after the prescribed period shall be dismissed, even if limitation has not been set up as a defence.
In the present case, the alleged disputed transactions/withdrawals pertains to the period from 21.12.2012 to 26.12.2012, whereas the present suit for recovery has been filed in the year 2020.

The present case is governed by Article 22 of the Limitation Act, 1963, which provides that where a relationship of banker and customer exists between the parties, the limitation period for filing a suit is three years.

It is further stated that the Plaintiffs have not placed any document before this Court to establish that they are the lawful legal heirs of the deceased Late Ms. Shakuntala Sethi (account holder of Account No. 13521010000074 with the Defendant Bank, Sabzi Mandi, Delhi).
In the entire plaint, the Plaintiffs have failed to place on record any document at the time of filing of the present suit to prove their status as legal heirs.
In the absence of such proof, this Court cannot presume that the Plaintiffs are the legal heirs of the deceased Late Ms. Shakuntala Sethi and are thus entitled to file the present suit.

It is further stated that, from the record available with the Defendant Bank, it is apparent that the grievance, if any, of the Plaintiffs lies CSDJ No. 275/2020 Ms. Poonam Verma &
Ors. Vs. HDFC Bank Page no 5/ 17 against the bearer of the cheques/cheque holder, namely Mr.
Amandeep Singh who is a necessary party as he got the cheque-bok issued on behalf of the account holder claiming to be the grandson of the account holder and approached the defendant bank along with identity proof of both the account holder and the authorized representative.
A written request for handover of the cheque book was also submitted at the said branch.

sentences.text: In response to the WS of the defendant, plaintiffs have filed the replication denying the averments made in the WS.
It is stated that the deceased account holder never applied for any such cheque book with the Defendant Bank and never made any request dated 15.12.2012 for issuance of a cheque book.

The deceased account holder also never authorized any person by the name of Mr.
Amandeep Singh, as alleged by the Defendant.
Thus, the question of issuing any such cheque book to the said alleged person does not arise at all.

In fact, the officials of the Defendant Bank themselves committed fraud and cheating with the Plaintiffs, and in order to embezzle the amount from the bank account of the deceased, they manipulated the alleged request letter, fabricated the signatures of the account holder, and carried out unauthorized transactions.

The said alleged person, Mr.
Amandeep Singh, is nothing but a fictitious creation of the officials of the Defendant Bank and has been introduced only to cover up their fraudulent acts.

11. It is argued on behalf of the plaintiff that defendant bank is liable to pay the suit amount to the plaintiff being LRs of the account holder i.e. Late Smt. Shakuntala Sethi as the officials of defendant bank have wrongly debited/embezzled the suit amount from the bank account of Smt. Shakuntala Sethi on 21.12.2022 and 26.12.2022.
No cheque book in respect of cheque nos.- 140008, 140007, 140006 and 140010 have been issued to Smt. Shakuntala sethi.
Sh. Amandeep Singh, who as per the stand of defendant got a new cheque-book issued on behalf of Smt. Shakuntala Sethi, is a fictitious person as he is not traceable as per the police report.

The entire burden is upon the defendant bank to show as to how the amount of Rs.12,49,000/-
have been debited from the account of Smt. Shaknutala Sethi.
12. On the other hand it is argued on behalf of the defendant that present suit is hopelessly time-barred.
As per para no. 4 of the plaint, the deceased mother of the Plaintiffs requested the bank statement of the account in question in January 2015 for income tax purposes.
In the same paragraph, the Plaintiffs CSDJ No. 275/2020 Ms. Poonam Verma & Ors.

Vs. HDFC Bank Page no 10/ 17 stated that upon obtaining the bank statement, the deceased, Smt. Shakuntla Sethi, was shocked to discover the embezzlement of Rs. 12,49,000/- from the aforesaid account during the period 21.12.2012 to 26.12.2012.
As per the said paragraph, the Plaintiffs had knowledge of the transactions in question as early as January 2015.

It is further argued that para 29 of the Plaint is again a classic example of clever drafting, wherein only the dates of filing an application under Section 156(3) Cr.P.C., a complaint under Section 200 Cr.P.C., and the status report filed by the police dated 05.07.2018 are mentioned, which, in any case, do not stop or extend the limitation period for filing a civil suit for recovery.

Further it is argued that police investigation found no negligence on the part of the bank during the criminal proceedings before the Court of Ld. JMFC-13,

colly.).
The report clearly records that the alleged accused, Mr. Amandeep Singh, could not be traced and no role whatsoever of the officials of the Defendant Bank was found.
Thus, even after investigation by the law enforcement authorities, no negligence, collusion, or misconduct on the part of the bank officials was established.

sentences.text: Plaintiffs failed to prove their locus standi.

The Plaintiffs claim to be the legal heirs of late Ms.
Shakuntla Sethi.
No documentary proof whatsoever, such as: a surviving member certificate, a legal heir certificate, or any document establishing parentage, has been placed on record.
The suit is bad on account of non- impleadment of the alleged wrongdoer.
The Plaintiffs themselves allege that the withdrawals were made by Mr. Amandeep Singh, who claimed to be the grandson of the deceased account holder.
Surprisingly, the Plaintiffs have not impleaded the said person as a party to the present suit.
13. In rebuttal, it is submitted on behalf of the plaintiff that affidavits of all the LRs of Shakuntala Sethi are on record.
So, there is no requirement of all the LRs of Smt. Shakuntal Sethi to step into the witness box.

14. My issue-wise findings are as under:
15. Issue no. 1 Whether the plaintiffs are entitled to decree for recovery of Rs. 12,49,000/- alongwith interest as prayed for?

OPP. 
Onus to prove this issues is upon the plaintiff.

The case of the plaintiffs is that the officials of the defendant made four unauthorized withdrawals amounting to Rs.12,49,000/- from the account of Smt. Shakuntala Sethi, who is the mother of Plaintiff No. 1.

The only witness examined by the plaintiffs in support of their claim is PW-1, Smt. Poonam Verma, daughter of the account holder,
i.e., Smt. Shakuntala Sethi.
In her examination-in-chief, she relied only upon her evidence affidavit Ex.PW1/1, and all the documents relied upon by her were merely photocopies.
Therefore, the same were de- CSDJ No. 275/2020 Ms. Poonam Verma & Ors.
Vs. HDFC Bank Page no 12/ 17 exhibited and marked as Mark A to Mark D.
No explanation is furnished as to why no original documents have been placed on record.

Admittedly, the plaintiffs came to know about the alleged illegal withdrawals from the account of Smt. Shakuntala Sethi sometime in January 2015, when the deceased herself requested the bank statement from the defendant bank for income tax purposes.
As per para no. 6 of the evidence affidavit Ex.PW1/1, a complaint was made to the defendant bank vide letter dated 10.03.2015.
However, neither the said letter dated 10.03.2015 nor any other record pertaining to proceedings initiated by Smt. Shakuntala Sethi or her legal representatives have been placed on record.
This fact was admitted by PW-1 in her cross-examination dated 09.05.2025.

Further, in her cross-examination recorded by the Ld. Local Commissioner, PW-1 could not specify the exact date of the visit made by Late Smt. Shakuntala Sethi along with her son to enquire about the alleged unauthorized withdrawals.
The defendant has also taken the plea that the present suit is time-barred in the written statement.

Even though no specific issue regarding limitation has been framed, it is the duty of the Court to determine whether the suit has been filed within the prescribed period of limitation, as mandated under Section 3 of the Limitation Act.
(Reference:"Ajaj Enterprises v. Jayant Vegoiles & Chemicals, AIR 1991 Bom 35". )

sentences.text: As per para no. 14 of the plaint, it is apparent that the plaintiffs were well aware of the alleged embezzlement by 02.07.2016, when all efforts made by Late Smt. Shakuntala Sethi and her son proved futile, and a police complaint was lodged on 02.07.2016.
In other words, the plaintiffs have CSDJ No. 275/2020 Ms. Poonam Verma & Ors.
Vs. HDFC Bank Page no 13/ 17 means to discover the fraud/ embezzlement by 02.07.2016 as per Section 17 (1) of the Limitation Act.
Admittedly, the period of limitation in the present suit is to be determined as per Article 22 of the Schedule to the Limitation Act, 1963.
As per Article 22, the limitation period is three years, which is to be reckoned from the date of demand made by the customer to the bank.

In the absence of any document on record showing when such demand for refund of the alleged illegal withdrawals was made by Late Smt. Shakuntala Sethi or her legal representatives, or any document to show as to how the fraud on the part of the defendant bank has been discovered by the plaintiffs, it can be reasonably inferred that such demand would have been made prior to 02.07.2016, i.e., the date on which the alleged police complaint was lodged at PS Swaroop Nagar.
The present suit was filed on 23.12.2020, which is beyond the prescribed period of limitation.

Thus, there is merit in the contention of the Ld.
Counsel for the defendant that the suit is time-barred.
17. In the written statement, it is claimed on behalf of the defendant that the amount in question was withdrawn by presenting four cheques bearing the signatures of Late Smt. Shakuntala Sethi.
It is further claimed that the cheque book was issued by the defendant bank on 15.12.2012 to one Amandeep Singh, who is stated to be the grandson of the deceased.
It is also claimed that, prior to handing over the cheque book, a verification call was made on the registered mobile number.

However, it is alleged that the said mobile number (9540405121) does not belong to Smt.
Shakuntala Sethi.
The defendant has also furnished the address details of Amandeep Singh in the written statement.
The plaintiffs, CSDJ No. 275/2020 Ms. Poonam Verma & Ors. Vs. HDFC Bank Page no 14/ 17 however, claim that the said Amandeep Singh is a fictitious person.

sentences.text: Despite this, no effort has been made by the plaintiffs to implead the said Amandeep Singh as a party to the present suit.

Further, no RBI guidelines regarding the issuance or handling of cheque books have been placed on record by the plaintiffs to show any foul play or negligence on the part of officials of defendant bank.
Even PW-1 admitted in her cross-examination that she was not aware of the relevant RBI policies and guidelines, as stated in para no. 9 of her evidence affidavit.

18. As per the untrace report filed by DW-2, Sh. Ankur, Assistant Ahlmad from the Court of Ms.
Rashi Raheja, Ld. JMFC-13, Central District, Tis Hazari Courts, Delhi, it is apparent that the defendant bank has furnished photocopies of the account opening form of Late Smt. Shakuntala Sethi as well as photocopies of the cheques on the basis of which the alleged withdrawals were made.

No efforts have been made by the plaintiffs to get the original documents summoned or to get the signatures of Late Smt. Shakuntala Sethi on the impugned cheques compared with her admitted signatures on the account opening form.
19. In these circumstances, in the opinion of this Court, the plaintiffs have failed to prove any negligence or foul play on the part of the officials of the defendant bank.
Accordingly, the plaintiffs are not entitled to recover any amount from the defendant bank.
Accordingly, this issue is decided in favour of the defendant and against the plaintiff.

21. Issue no. 3
Whether plaintiffs have no locus standi to file the present suit?
OPD Onus to prove this issues is upon the defendant.
The present suit has been filed by the sons and daughters of Late Smt. Shakuntala Sethi, who was an account holder with the defendant bank.
However, the plaint has been filed only by one legal representative, namely Smt. Poonam Verma.
No affidavit or Power of Attorney on behalf of the other legal representatives has been filed or exhibited during the evidence of PW-1.

The plaint appears to have been instituted solely by Smt. Poonam Verma, and no affidavits of the other legal representatives have either been filed along with the plaint or got exhibited during the course of evidence.
The defendant has specifically raised an objection that there is no document on record to establish that the plaintiffs are the legal representatives of Late Smt. Shakuntala Sethi.
Despite such objection, no documents have been filed by the plaintiffs to prove that they are the legal representatives of Late Smt. Shakuntala Sethi.
Accordingly, this issue is decided in favour of the defendant and against the plaintiffs.
22. Issue no. 4
Whether no cause of action has arisen in favour of plaintiffs to file the present suit?
OPD Onus to prove this issues is upon the defendant.

It is well settled that only averments made in the plaint are to be CSDJ No. 275/2020 Ms. Poonam Verma & Ors. Vs. HDFC Bank Page no 16/ 17 considered, and the defence set up in the WS is not required to be looked into to determine the cause of action.

It is further submitted that the Limitation Act, 1963 clearly provides that every suit instituted, appeal preferred, or application made after the prescribed period shall be dismissed, even if limitation has not been set up as a defence.
In the present case, the alleged disputed transactions/withdrawals pertains to the period from 21.12.2012 to 26.12.2012, whereas the present suit for recovery has been filed in the year 2020.
The present case is governed by Article 22 of the Limitation Act, 1963, which provides that where a relationship of banker and customer exists between the parties, the limitation period for filing a suit is three years.

opennyai_summary.arguments:
11. It is argued on behalf of the plaintiff that defendant bank is liable to pay the suit amount to the plaintiff being LRs of the account holder i.e. Late Smt. Shakuntala Sethi as the officials of defendant bank have wrongly debited/embezzled the suit amount from the bank account of Smt. Shakuntala Sethi on 21.12.2022 and 26.12.2022.
Sh. Amandeep Singh, who as per the stand of defendant got a new cheque-book issued on behalf of Smt. Shakuntala Sethi, is a fictitious person as he is not traceable as per the police report.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Thus, even after investigation by the law enforcement authorities, no negligence, collusion, or misconduct on the part of the bank officials was established.
In the absence of any proof of negligence, the very foundation of the Plaintiffs' claim collapses.
(Reference:"Ajaj Enterprises v. Jayant Vegoiles & Chemicals, AIR 1991 Bom 35". )

7 16.
Admittedly, the period of limitation in the present suit is to be determined as per Article 22 of the Schedule to the Limitation Act, 1963.
In the absence of any document on record showing when such demand for refund of the alleged illegal withdrawals was made by Late Smt. Shakuntala Sethi or her legal representatives, or any document to show as to how the fraud on the part of the defendant bank has been discovered by the plaintiffs, it can be reasonably inferred that such demand would have been made prior to 02.07.2016, i.e., the date on which the alleged police complaint was lodged at PS Swaroop Nagar.
The present suit was filed on 23.12.2020, which is beyond the prescribed period of limitation.
Further, no RBI guidelines regarding the issuance or handling of cheque books have been placed on record by the plaintiffs to show any foul play or negligence on the part of officials of defendant bank.
No efforts have been made by the plaintiffs to get the original documents summoned or to get the signatures of Late Smt. Shakuntala Sethi on the impugned cheques compared with her admitted signatures on the account opening form.
19. In these circumstances, in the opinion of this Court, the plaintiffs have failed to prove any negligence or foul play on the part of the officials of the defendant bank.
Accordingly, the plaintiffs are not entitled to recover any amount from the defendant bank.
However, the plaint has been filed only by one legal representative, namely Smt. Poonam Verma.
No affidavit or Power of Attorney on behalf of the other legal representatives has been filed or exhibited during the evidence of PW-1.
The defendant has specifically raised an objection that there is no document on record to establish that the plaintiffs are the legal representatives of Late Smt. Shakuntala Sethi.
